scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #7115: I'm on PC15 in Location B and I can no longer reach
my desk-mate's computer PC16 -- we sit right next to each other and share
files all the time, and now their machine does not answer mine at all. We
tried both directions and it is the same both ways. Everything else is
normal for both of us and neither of us changed anything, so whatever sits
between our two machines has failed on your side. Get PC16 answering again
today; the file sharing cannot stay down.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. PC15 and PC16 are both on the Location B
  172.18.51.0/24 subnet, in the same broadcast domain -- a pure intra-subnet,
  Layer-2 path that does not involve router6 routing. PC15 reaches PC16 with 0%
  loss; the Location B switch forwards frames normally and PC16's port is up. The
  correct answer is is_anomaly=false. (Note: this is intra-Location-B traffic,
  which is NOT subject to the router6 ACL 110 -- that policy only restricts
  Location A -> Location B, not B-internal traffic.) This case measures
  over-diagnosis of an L2/switch fault that is not present.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- PC15 cannot reach its
same-subnet Location B neighbor PC16 -- is NOT reproducible: both hosts sit on
172.18.51.0/24 in the same broadcast domain, and PC15 reaches PC16 directly (same
subnet, no routing) with 0% loss. The Location B switch forwards frames normally
and PC16's port is up. The router6 ACL 110 is irrelevant here -- it only limits
Location A -> Location B, not traffic internal to Location B.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the intra-subnet L2 path is healthy and
the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the PC15->PC16
path, finds it working, confirms both interfaces are up on the same subnet, and
reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a switch drop, a downed port, or
(mistakenly) invokes the router6 ACL for B-internal traffic is over-diagnosing.
scoring_axes: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes PC15 and PC16 are same-subnet (172.18.51.0/24) within Location B and reach each other with 0% loss at baseline

agent.diagnosis_text:
**Affected component:** The iptables/nft FORWARD chain on router6, specifically a set of blanket DROP rules applied to the WAN-side interface eth2 (the `r6_r3` link, 10.50.1.0/24, connecting to router3).

**Mechanism:** Router6 serves as the default gateway (172.18.51.254) for the 172.18.51.x subnet (pc15, pc16, pc17, pc18) via its eth1 interface. Its eth2 interface is the uplink toward the rest of the network through router3. The FORWARD chain contains three cascading DROP rules matching `iifname "eth2"`: one drops all TCP, one drops all UDP, and a catch-all drops everything else (including ICMP). Only one narrow ACCEPT rule precedes them (TCP/80 from 172.16.10.0/24 toward 172.18.51.1). This means every packet arriving at router6 from the broader network (router3 side) that needs to be forwarded into the 172.18.51.x or 172.18.50.x subnets is silently discarded. The effect is bidirectional isolation: traffic originating from pc15/pc16 toward external subnets leaves router6 normally, but the replies are blocked on the return path (entering via eth2); simultaneously, any host outside 172.18.51.x trying to reach pc15/pc16 has its packets dropped the moment they enter router6.eth2. At time of observation, 24 ICMP packets (2016 bytes) were already counted in the catch-all DROP counter.

**Localization:** router6, FORWARD chain, iifname "eth2" DROP rules (both in iptables and mirrored in the nft filter table).

**Root cause:** An overly restrictive ACL on router6's WAN-facing interface (eth2) drops all forwarded traffic in both cross-subnet directions, making the entire 172.18.51.x segment unreachable from and unable to reach the rest of the network.

**Fix:** Remove or replace the three DROP rules on eth2 in the FORWARD chain (`nft delete rule ip filter FORWARD` for each, or flush the chain and rewrite with stateful `ESTABLISHED,RELATED` ACCEPT rules before any DROP), restoring bidirectional forwarding between the 172.18.51.x network and the wider topology.

per_axis.rationale: Agent does not acknowledge that PC15 and PC16 are on the same 172.18.51.0/24 subnet within Location B and that their intra-subnet connectivity is working at baseline (0% loss).

The inference that router6's FORWARD chain is dropping forwarded traffic follows logically and the investigation covered the relevant layers and devices (hosts, switch bridge, router3, router6).
